consistency_checks.detail: Urine bilirubin (severity 4) is not adequately explained by any diagnosis in the original differential.
Adjusted probabilities have been calibrated to sum to approximately 1.0.

critical_findings_addressed: Metabolic acidosis pattern (low CO₂, high Cl⁻, borderline high K⁺)
critical_findings_missed: Urine bilirubin 0.8 mg/dL (positive) – not convincingly explained
top_concerns: Unexplained bilirubinuria suggesting an unaddressed hepatic or hemolytic disorder
Probability calibration for several diagnoses (diabetes, NAFLD, RTA)
Missing liver work‑up to clarify NAFLD vs. cholestasis/hemolysis
review_summary: The junior differential captures the major renal and metabolic issues but under‑estimates the likelihood of diabetes and type 4 RTA, over‑estimates NAFLD/NASH, and fails to explain bilirubinuria. Adjusted probabilities and added diagnoses (distinct type 4 RTA and a separate hepatic/hemolytic work‑up) improve alignment with the raw evidence. Addressing the highlighted gaps—especially confirming diabetes and investigating bilirubinuria—will be critical for accurate diagnosis and management.
